{{short description|Triangle center: symmedian point of the triangle's excentral triangle}}
[[File:Mandart inellipse - resized.svg|thumb|300px|
{{legend-line|solid #333333|Arbitrary triangle}}
{{legend-line|solid red|[[Mandart inellipse]] (centered at the '''mittenpunkt''' {{mvar|M}})}}
{{legend-line|solid blue|Lines from the triangle's [[excenter]]s to each corresponding edge midpoint ([[Concurrent lines|concurrent]] at the '''mittenpunkt''' {{mvar|M}})}}
{{legend-line|solid lime|[[Splitter (geometry)|Splitters]] of the triangle (concurrent at the [[Nagel point]] {{mvar|N}})}}]]

In [[geometry]], the {{lang|de|'''mittenpunkt'''|italic=no}} (from [[German language|German]]: ''middle point'') of a [[triangle]] is a [[triangle center]]: a point defined from the triangle that is invariant under [[Euclidean transformation]]s of the triangle. It was identified in 1836 by [[Christian Heinrich von Nagel]] as the [[symmedian]] point of the [[excentral triangle]] of the given triangle.<ref name="k94">{{citation
 | last = Kimberling | first = Clark
 | issue = 3
 | journal = Mathematics Magazine
 | jstor = 2690608
 | mr = 1573021
 | pages = 163–187
 | title = Central Points and Central Lines in the Plane of a Triangle
 | volume = 67
 | year = 1994
 | doi=10.2307/2690608}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = v. Nagel | first = C. H. | author-link = Christian Heinrich von Nagel
 | location = Leipzig
 | title = Untersuchungen über die wichtigsten zum Dreiecke gehörenden Kreise
 | year = 1836}}.</ref>

==Coordinates==
The mittenpunkt has [[trilinear coordinates]]<ref name="k94"/>
:<math>(b+c-a): (c+a-b ):(a+b-c)</math>
where {{mvar|a}}, {{mvar|b}}, and {{mvar|c}} are the side lengths of the given triangle.
Expressed instead in terms of the angles {{mvar|A}}, {{mvar|B}}, and {{mvar|C}}, the trilinears are<ref name= Enc>http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers</ref>
:<math>\cot \frac{A}{2} : \cot \frac{B}{2} : \cot \frac{C}{2}=(\csc A+\cot A):(\csc B+\cot B):(\csc C+\cot C).</math>

The [[barycentric coordinates (mathematics)|barycentric coordinates]] are<ref name=Enc/>

:<math>a(b+c-a):b(c+a-b):c(a+b-c) = (1+\cos A):(1+\cos B):(1+\cos C).</math>

==Collinearities==

The mittenpunkt is at the intersection of the line connecting the [[centroid]] and the [[Gergonne point]], the line connecting the [[incenter]] and the [[symmedian point]] and the line connecting the [[orthocenter]] with the [[Spieker center]], thus establishing three [[collinear points|collinearities]] involving the mittenpunkt.<ref>Paul Yiu, "The uses of homogeneous barycentric coordinates in plane euclidean geometry" http://lya.fciencias.unam.mx/gfgf/ga20071/data/material/barycentricpaper.pdf</ref>

==Related figures==
The three lines connecting the excenters of the given triangle to the corresponding edge midpoints all meet at the mittenpunkt; thus, it is the [[perspective (geometry)|center of perspective]] of the excentral triangle and the median triangle, with the [[Desargues' theorem|corresponding axis of perspective]] being the trilinear polar of the [[Gergonne point]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Eddy | first = Roland H.
 | issue = 3
 | journal = [[Elemente der Mathematik]]
 | mr = 999636
 | pages = 79–80
 | title = A Desarguesian dual for Nagel's middlespoint
 | url = http://eudml.org/doc/141457
 | volume = 44
 | year = 1989}}.</ref> The mittenpunkt is also the [[centroid]] of the [[Mandart inellipse]] of the given triangle, the ellipse tangent to the triangle at its [[Extouch triangle|extouch points]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Gibert
 | first = Bernard
 | journal = Forum Geometricorum
 | mr = 2130231
 | pages = 177–198
 | title = Generalized Mandart conics
 | url = http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2004volume4/FG200421.pdf
 | volume = 4
 | year = 2004
 | access-date = 2012-09-02
 | archive-date = 2016-03-03
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233848/http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2004volume4/FG200421.pdf
 | url-status = dead
 }}.</ref>

The mittenpunkt also serves as the [[Gergonne point]] of the [[medial triangle]].
